skills.name: Solve quadratic equations using the quadratic formula

note.text:
The quadratic formula solves any quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0:
x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac)) / 2a.
Steps: rearrange to ax² + bx + c = 0; write down a, b, c with signs; work out b² − 4ac; take its square root; work out the two roots, one with + and one with −; round at the end.
Example: 2x² + 3x − 4 = 0: b² − 4ac = 9 + 32 = 41, so x = (−3 ± √41)/4, x ≈ 0.85 or x ≈ −2.35.
Divide the whole top by 2a, not just the square root.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text:
By the end, you should be able to solve any quadratic equation with the formula, giving exact roots or roots to {2} decimal places.
Builds on: Lesson {9} (where the formula comes from) and Lesson {7} (rearranging and rejecting roots).
Leads to: the discriminant and the nature of roots, and solving word problems in physics and business.

sections.heading: Traps to avoid
sections.text:
• −b changes the sign of b: if b = {-6}, then −b = {6}.
• −{4}ac with a negative c becomes a plus: c = {-4} gives −{4} × {2} × {br(-4)} = +{32}.
• The whole top is divided by {2}a: ({-3} + √{41})/{4}, not {-3} + √{41}/{4}.
• Rearrange first: x(x + {3}) = {5} is {quad(1, 3, -5)} = {0}, so c = {-5}.
If b² − {4}ac is negative there are no real roots: the calculator gives an error for the square root.

key_words.meaning: digits after the decimal point; {2} d.p. means hundredths
left as a surd or fraction, not rounded

mistake.why: The fraction line goes under the whole top. Work out {-3} + √{41} first, then divide by {4}.

worked_example.problem: Solve {quad(a, b, c)} = {0}, giving the roots to {2} decimal places.
worked_example.answer: x ≈ {roundTo((-b + sqrt(b * b - 4 * a * c)) / (2 * a), 0.01)} or x ≈ {roundTo((-b - sqrt(b * b - 4 * a * c)) / (2 * a), 0.01)}

cards.idea: When b² − {4}ac is a square number, the roots are exact.
Otherwise use a calculator for the square root and round only at the end.
Divide the whole top by {2}a, not only the square root.

check.prompt: Solve {quad(a, b, c)} = {0}. Give the smaller root to {2} decimal places.
check.answer: roundTo((-b - sqrt(b * b - 4 * a * c)) / (2 * a), 0.01)

misconceptions.wrong: roundTo((-b + sqrt(b * b - 4 * a * c)) / (2 * a), 0.01)
misconceptions.explain: That is the larger root (with +). The smaller one uses −.

misconceptions.wrong: roundTo((b - sqrt(b * b - 4 * a * c)) / (2 * a), 0.01)
roundTo((-b - sqrt(b * b - 4 * a * c)) / a, 0.01)
misconceptions.explain: Divide by {2}a = {2 * a}, not by a.

solution: The smaller root uses −: x = ({-b} − √{b * b - 4 * a * c}) / {2 * a}.

questions.prompt: Use the quadratic formula to solve {quad(1, -(p + q), p * q)} = {0}. Give the larger root.

misconceptions.explain: Divide the whole top by {2}a = {2}: ({p + q} + {abs(p - q)}) / {2}.
−b = {p + q}, not {-(p + q)}: the sign of b changes.

solution: b² − {4}ac = {(p + q) * (p + q)} − {4 * p * q} = {(p - q) * (p - q)}, and its square root is {abs(p - q)}.
The larger root is ({p + q} + {abs(p - q)}) / {2} = {answer}.

questions.prompt: Solve x({poly([1, 'x'], [b, ''])}) = {k}. Give the positive root to {2} decimal places.

misconceptions.explain: Moving {k} to the left makes c = {-k}, so −{4}ac = +{4 * k}.

solution: Expand and make one side {0}: {quad(1, b, -k)} = {0}.

questions.prompt: A ball is thrown up from a cliff. After t seconds its height above the sea is h = {u}t − {5}t² + {s} metres. Use the quadratic formula to find when it reaches the sea (h = {0}). Give t to {2} decimal places.

misconceptions.explain: That root is negative: the ball cannot reach the sea before it is thrown.

solution: t = ({u} ± √{u * u + 20 * s}) / {10}. Time cannot be negative, so take +.
